description: BAT41 small-signal Schottky (100 V): a low clipper, between germanium and silicon (our fit to Vishay's sheet)

source.licence: Our own fit to the maker's datasheet curve (D-156): the values are Solum Builder's

rating_sources.if_avg: Vishay BAT41 data sheet, Rev. 2.1, 07-Nov-2024 (doc 85659): Forward continuous current 100 mA
rating_sources.vr_max: Vishay BAT41 data sheet, Rev. 2.1, 07-Nov-2024 (doc 85659): Repetitive peak reverse voltage 100 V

fit.figure: Fig. 3 - Typical Forward Current vs. Forward Voltage, Tj = 25 °C (blue), read from the PDF's vector drawing
fit.method: Two diodes in parallel (scripts/fit_models.py fit_diode_pair, D-159): the first fitted, as one diode is, to the points up to 4 mA; the second to the current the points above that carry beyond the first; Both IS held under the sheet's 100 nA reverse-current limit at 50 V; CJO is the sheet's 2 pF at 1 V; BV 100 V at 100 µA, the sheet's breakdown test, on the first diode
fit.note: The sheet's curve rises 0.32 V from 1 to 10 mA but only 0.18 V from 10 to 100 mA, which one diode can't follow (97 mV off at best), so the model is two diodes in parallel (D-159). A subcircuit, like the zeners: its current isn't read at the operating point (D-155)
